chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, raising it, said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would say during a bereavement: 'Praise is to Allah who did not make my bereavement in my religion, and praise is to Allah who, had He willed, could have made my bereavement greater than what it was, and praise is to Allah for the matter which He willed to be, and it was.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to say when facing a loss or bereavement in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a specific etiquette for bereavement, prioritizing spiritual preservation over material loss. It reflects the Shia theological emphasis on *rida* (contentment) with divine decree, framing suffering as a test of faith rather than a punishment, thereby encouraging believers to view calamities through the lens of gratitude (*shukr*).
